newsitem.title: USA: Mexico interest rates likely to drop -Bear Stearns.
newsitem.headline: Mexico interest rates likely to drop -Bear Stearns.

text.p: Mexican interest rates are likely to drop in coming months following landmark elections, a Bear Stearns analyst said Monday.
David Malpass, Bear Stearns' director for international economics, said Mexican banks could benefit from falling interest rates and the perception that the Sunday vote went smoothly.
"We think that Mexico will be able to see some interest rate cuts in July and August to the extent that the elections came out within expectations," Malpass said in a telephone conference call.

He said "significant" inflows of money in March, April and May "were not fully reflected in interest rate cuts, in part because (Mexican authorities) don't want to have the perception that monetary policy was being ... used to affect the election."

Results showed the Institutional Revolutionary Party (PRI) lost its 68-year grip on the Chamber of Deputies, the lower house of Congress. It was also beaten in the first race for Mexico City mayor this century by leftist Cuauhtemoc Cardenas of the Party of the Democratic Revolution (PRD).
In response to the election, Mexican overnight Cetes rates opened down sharply but then gave up some of those gains to trade down 180 basis points at 18.85 percent.

Delal Baer, a Mexico expert at Washington's Center for Strategic and International Studies, said Congress was likely to continue to support President Ernesto Zedillo's economic reforms despite the strong showing by the PRD and the rightist National Action Party (PAN).
"The basic logic of the stable Congress that is able to pass fundamental economic reform and preserve fiscal stability and responsibility is still in place," she said.
"... There's nothing in the makeup of this Congress that would prevent the passage of responsible budgets and even continue the process of economic reform."
With 80 percent of the vote counted in the lower house race, the PRI had 38.23 percent, short of the 42.2 percent needed to keep its majority. The PAN had 27.31 percent and the PRD won 25.22 percent.
